newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak finmin sees technology boosting imports.
newsitem.headline: Slovak finmin sees technology boosting imports.

text.p: Slovak Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said on Wednesday he expected imports to continue growing this year, mainly due to technology imports for projects such as the Mochovce nuclear power plant.
"On the other hand, we expect further acceleration in exports, mainly in goods with higher added value such as cars," Kozlik said.
In first two months 1997, Slovakia's exports totalled 45.373 billion crowns, up 13.1 percent from January-February 1996. This compared with a 9 percent year-on-year rise in January 1997.

Imports, led by a 19.9 percent rise in fossil fuels and mineral oils, rose 5.4 percent year-on-year in the first two months of 1997, totalling 56.193 billion crowns, compared with 22.3 percent year-on-year growth in January.

Kozlik earlier said the trade deficit was 15.9 billion crowns in the first quarter of this year, compared with 15.7 billion in the first quarter of 1996. He gave no detailed breakdown of imports or exports.
